

```{r}

smote_impl <- function(df, var, k, over_ratio, call = caller_env()) {
  data <- split(df, df[[var]])
  majority_count <- max(table(df[[var]]))
  ratio_target <- majority_count * over_ratio
  which_upsample <- which(table(df[[var]]) < ratio_target)
  samples_needed <- ratio_target - table(df[[var]])[which_upsample]
  min_names <- names(samples_needed)

  out_dfs <- list()

  for (i in seq_along(samples_needed)) {
    minority_df <- data[[min_names[i]]]
    minority <- as.matrix(minority_df[names(minority_df) != var])

    if (nrow(minority) <= k) {
      cli::cli_abort("Not enough observations of {.val {min_names[i]}} to perform SMOTE.", call = call)
    }

    synthetic <- smote_data(minority, k = k, n_samples = samples_needed[i])
    out_df <- as.data.frame(synthetic)
    names(out_df) <- setdiff(names(df), var)
    out_df_nrow <- min(nrow(out_df), 1)
    out_df[var] <- data[[names(samples_needed)[i]]][[var]][out_df_nrow]
    out_df <- out_df[names(df)]
    out_dfs[[i]] <- out_df
  }

  final <- rbind(df, do.call(rbind, out_dfs))
  final[[var]] <- factor(final[[var]], levels = levels(df[[var]]))
  rownames(final) <- NULL
  final
}

```


```{r}
smote_data <- function(data, k, n_samples, smote_ids = seq_len(nrow(data))) {
  ids <- RANN::nn2(data, k = k + 1, searchtype = "priority")$nn.idx
  indexes <- rep(sample(smote_ids), length.out = n_samples)
  index_len <- tabulate(indexes, NROW(data))
  out <- matrix(0, nrow = n_samples, ncol = ncol(data))
  sampleids <- sample.int(k, n_samples, TRUE)
  runif_ids <- stats::runif(n_samples)

  iii <- 0
  for (row_num in smote_ids) {
    index_selection <- iii + seq_len(index_len[row_num])
    # removes itself as nearest neighbour
    id_knn <- ids[row_num, ids[row_num, ] != row_num]
    dif <- data[id_knn[sampleids[index_selection]], ] -
      data[rep(row_num, index_len[row_num]), ]
    gap <- dif * runif_ids[index_selection]
    out[index_selection, ] <- data[rep(row_num, index_len[row_num]), ] + gap
    iii <- iii + index_len[row_num]
  }

  out
}

```

# Synthetic Data

```{r make-data}
set.seed(42)

# 100 majority rows (class = "cat"), 20 minority rows (class = "dog")
# All numeric predictors, no NAs, factor class column — passes all checks
df <- data.frame(
  x     = c(rnorm(100, mean = 0), rnorm(20, mean = 5)),
  y     = c(rnorm(100, mean = 0), rnorm(20, mean = 5)),
  class = factor(c(rep("cat", 100), rep("dog", 20)))
)

cat("Shape:", nrow(df), "rows x", ncol(df), "cols\n")
table(df$class)   # cat=100, dog=20
```

---

# Test `smote_data()` — the geometry core

```{r test-smote-data}
# Inputs:
#   data     : numeric matrix [20 x 2]  (just the dog rows, no label)
#   k        : 5 nearest neighbors
#   n_samples: 80  (we want 80 synthetic points)

minority_matrix <- as.matrix(df[df$class == "dog", c("x", "y")])
cat("minority_matrix shape:", nrow(minority_matrix), "x", ncol(minority_matrix), "\n")
# [20 x 2] — rows=minority points, cols=x,y

synthetic_matrix <- smote_data(
  data      = minority_matrix,
  k         = 5,
  n_samples = 80
)

cat("synthetic_matrix shape:", nrow(synthetic_matrix), "x", ncol(synthetic_matrix), "\n")
# Expected: [80 x 2] — 80 new synthetic points, same 2 features

# Sanity check: synthetic points should fall between real dog points
cat("Real dog x range    :", range(minority_matrix[, 1]), "\n")
cat("Synthetic x range   :", range(synthetic_matrix[, 1]), "\n")
# Synthetic range should be *inside* real range (interpolation, not extrapolation)
```

---

# Test `smote_impl()` — the orchestrator

```{r test-smote-impl}
# smote_impl() takes the full df, balances it
# over_ratio = 1 means: bring minority up to majority count (100)
# so it needs to generate 100 - 20 = 80 synthetic "dog" rows

result_impl <- smote_impl(
  df         = df,
  var        = "class",
  k          = 5,
  over_ratio = 1
)

cat("Original shape :", nrow(df),          "rows\n")
cat("Balanced shape :", nrow(result_impl), "rows\n")
# Expected: 100 (original) + 80 (synthetic dog) = 180 rows

table(result_impl$class)
# Expected: cat=100, dog=100

# Check no NAs were introduced
cat("NAs in result:", sum(is.na(result_impl)), "\n")

# Check factor levels preserved
cat("Factor levels:", levels(result_impl$class), "\n")
```

---

# Test `smote()` — the full public function (with checks)

```{r test-smote}
# smote() is the same as smote_impl() but validates inputs first.
# Our df was designed to pass all checks:
#   check_data_frame : df is a data.frame         ✓
#   check_var        : "class" exists in df       ✓
#   check_number_whole(k=5, min=1)                ✓
#   check_number_decimal(over_ratio=1)            ✓
#   check_numeric    : x and y are numeric        ✓
#   check_na         : no missing values          ✓

result_smote <- smote(df, var = "class", k = 5, over_ratio = 1)

cat("smote() output shape:", nrow(result_smote), "rows\n")
table(result_smote$class)
# Same as smote_impl() result: cat=100, dog=100
```

# Extra: test edge cases

```{r test-edge-cases}
# --- over_ratio = 0.5: bring dog up to 50% of cat (50 rows) ---
result_half <- smote(df, var = "class", k = 5, over_ratio = 0.5)
cat("over_ratio=0.5 :", "\n")
print(table(result_half$class))
# Expected: cat=100, dog=50

# --- k = 10: more neighbors used for interpolation ---
result_k10 <- smote(df, var = "class", k = 10, over_ratio = 1)
cat("k=10 result    :", "\n")
print(table(result_k10$class))
# Same counts, different synthetic point positions

# --- three-class imbalance ---
df3 <- data.frame(
  x     = c(rnorm(100), rnorm(30, 5), rnorm(10, -5)),
  y     = c(rnorm(100), rnorm(30, 5), rnorm(10, -5)),
  class = factor(c(rep("cat", 100), rep("dog", 30), rep("bird", 10)))
)
result3 <- smote(df3, var = "class", k = 5, over_ratio = 1)
cat("Three-class result:\n")
print(table(result3$class))
# Expected: cat=100, dog=100, bird=100
```

# Visualise before vs after

```{r plot, fig.width=10, fig.height=4}
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))

# Before
plot(df$x, df$y,
     col  = ifelse(df$class == "cat", "steelblue", "tomato"),
     pch  = 16, main = "Before SMOTE",
     xlab = "x", ylab = "y")
legend("topright", legend = c("cat (100)", "dog (20)"),
       col = c("steelblue", "tomato"), pch = 16)

# After
plot(result_smote$x, result_smote$y,
     col  = ifelse(result_smote$class == "cat", "steelblue", "tomato"),
     pch  = 16, main = "After SMOTE",
     xlab = "x", ylab = "y")
legend("topright", legend = c("cat (100)", "dog (100)"),
       col = c("steelblue", "tomato"), pch = 16)
```

```{r}
# U-shaped distribution on [0,1] ("inverse bell curve")

# --- Parameters for U-shape ---
a <- 1.   # shape1 < 1
b <- 1.   # shape2 < 1

# Generate sample
n <- 10000
set.seed(123)
x_u <- rbeta(n, a, b)

# Plot density of the U-shaped distribution
curve(dbeta(x, a, b), from = 0, to = 1, n = 1001,
      main = "Beta(0.5, 0.5) – U-shaped (inverse bell curve)",
      ylab = "Density", col = "blue", lwd = 2)
rug(x_u, col = "lightblue")
```

```{r}


# --- How to make the same function uniform? ---
# Option 1: Change the Beta parameters to (1, 1)
x_unif1 <- rbeta(n, 1, 1)   # Beta(1,1) = Uniform(0,1)

# Option 2: Probability integral transform:
# If X ~ Beta(0.5,0.5), then F(X) ~ Uniform(0,1) where F = pbeta
x_unif2 <- pbeta(x_u, a, b)

# Check: both should look uniform in histogram
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
hist(x_unif1, breaks = 30, probability = TRUE, main = "Beta(1,1)",
     xlab = "x", col = "gray80")
curve(dunif(x, 0, 1), add = TRUE, col = "red", lwd = 2)

hist(x_unif2, breaks = 30, probability = TRUE, main = "pbeta(X) where X ~ Beta(0.5,0.5)",
     xlab = "x", col = "gray80")
curve(dunif(x, 0, 1), add = TRUE, col = "red", lwd = 2)
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```
